transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-05
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~45m
Attendees: Ava Mitchell (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Maya Patel (Lynx Head of Search), Ethan Cole (ML Eng), Jordan Li (CTO)

Summary: quick discovery focused on embeddings + reranking architecture, vector DB integration (weaviate/pinecone/faiss options), throughput targets, and security/VPC requirements. Customer leaning toward Dedicated for predictable latency but wants Hosted as fallback.

Topics: embeddings dimensionality, hybrid search (bm25 + embed rerank), indexing throughput, bulk ingest, quantization, caching, Dedicated vs Hosted networking, SOC2/KMS questions.

00:00:03 Ava: Hey everyone thanks for joining, quick intros — I'm Ava, AE on the account and Diego our SE.
00:00:12 Maya: Hi all, Maya here, I run search at Lynx. We handle enterprise search for our customers, mostly technical docs and support articles, want to improve relevance with embeddings and a reranking stage.
00:00:25 Ethan: Ethan, ML eng — I own the ingestion pipeline and current vector infra.
00:00:30 Jordan: Jordan, CTO, listening in — main ask is predictable latency and security.

00:01:05 Diego: Great. Can you share current stack? What vector db and embedding model are you on?
00:01:14 Maya: Right now we use OpenSearch with a hybrid approach — bm25 first pass then some custom scoring. We're prototyping embeddings generated with text-embedding-3-small (1536) and storing vectors in a FAISS cluster running on k8s. It's been ok but scaling indexing and consistent latency in peak hours is painful.
00:01:45 Ava: Good context. Typical Qs: doc corpus size, queries per second, latency SLOs, and retention/compliance needs.
00:01:52 Ethan: Corpus is roughly 1.2M docs, typical query load 200-300 QPS with spikes to 1k QPS during business hours. Latency target is p95 < 120ms for the retriever+rerank end-to-end — ideally < 200ms including rerank.
00:02:10 Diego: Okay. For that topology most customers use a hybrid stack: fast vector index for recall (HNSW/IVF) plus a lightweight reranker model. We need to decide whether to host vectors in Pinecone/Weaviate or use Redwood's managed index on Dedicated.
00:02:28 Maya: Two things: cost and control. We can't send raw customer PII out for hosted unless it's encrypted and audited. Also need SOC2-type — sorry, we need SOC2 Type II and KMS support.
00:02:42 Ava: Understood. Redwood Dedicated supports VPC peering or private link and customer-managed KMS for encryption at rest; we also have audit logs and can provide SOC2 docs. We'll share the security packet.
00:03:00 Jordan: For Dedicated, do we still use our existing FAISS k8s or does Redwood host the vector store?
00:03:10 Diego: We can do both. Many teams keep their vector store and use Redwood for embeddings + rerank inference, others migrate vectors to Redwood-managed indexes for lower operational overhead. For high QPS the managed index on Dedicated gives much more predictable tail latency because it's co-located with the inference runtime.
00:03:35 Ethan: How about dimensionality — we're evaluating 1536 vs 768. Storage and index size matter — 1536 gives better retrieval quality but doubles storage and increases index search time. Any guidance?
00:03:50 Diego: Typical tradeoff. For our models we've seen diminishing returns beyond 1536 for text-heavy content; 768 often performs well for trimmed use cases. For latency/throughput, quantized 1536 with int8 or 4-bit schemes reduces footprint dramatically. On Redwood Dedicated we offer quantized execution paths and compressed vectors in the index.
00:04:20 Ava: Also worth noting rerank models matter: a small cross-encoder reranker with limited input length can boost MRR a lot and is usually only a small latency add if batched properly.
00:04:35 Maya: Can you explain batching behavior? We can't have rerank add 200ms per request.
00:04:42 Diego: Sure. Redwood runtime uses continuous batching and KV caching for decoder models; for rerank cross-encoders we do micro-batching with predictable latency SLOs. On Dedicated you can configure max batch latency and size; we can guarantee p95 if you set capacity appropriately.
00:05:05 Ethan: What about hybrid search architecture? We currently run BM25 then embedding recall then our reranker. Would you suggest moving to embedding-first or keep BM25 fallback?
00:05:18 Diego: Hybrid is pragmatic — BM25 ensures recall for long-tail queries and anchored tokens. Embedding recall catches semantic matches. Many teams run BM25 as a cheap filter, then embedding-based recall on the filtered set, then rerank. That reduces vector QPS. We can also support vector-only pipelines if you accept a denser index and retune.
00:05:43 Maya: On throughput — our ingest pipeline pushes 10k docs/day and occasional reindexing of 200k. Can Redwood's Dedicated handle bulk ingest? How do you time index rebuilds?
00:05:56 Diego: Dedicated supports parallel bulk ingest with backpressure; we provide ingestion endpoints and recommend using batched bulk writes. For big reindexes we recommend staging cluster or rolling index updates; indexing throughput depends on dim and indexing mode (HNSW rebuild vs incremental IVFPQ). We'll include numbers in the benchmark sheet.
00:06:18 Ethan: Any native connectors for OpenSearch/Elasticsearch so we can migrate metadata and text fields?
00:06:24 Ava: Yes, we have connectors and can help with migration scripts; also many customers keep OpenSearch for metadata-search and use Redwood indexes for embeddings.
00:06:40 Ethan: Latency numbers — do you have example p95 for retriever+rerank at 500 QPS on Dedicated?
00:06:48 Diego: Ballpark: retriever latency p95 for 1536-dim HNSW on Dedicated ~20-40ms, cross-encoder rerank batched p95 ~50-80ms depending on batch config, so combined you can see under 150ms with proper capacity. We'll send specific benchmark CSV.
00:07:08 Maya: That's promising. Cost — how does Dedicated pricing work vs hosted?
00:07:15 Ava: Hosted is per-token / per-embed usage; Dedicated is a reserved capacity model (monthly) with commit tiers and burst. For sustained high QPS Dedicated is usually cheaper and more predictable. We'll send model of cost estimates vs your traffic.
00:07:30 Jordan: Security follow-up: can we bring our own KMS? And do you support VPC peering or private link for limited egress?
00:07:39 Diego: Yes to both: customer-managed KMS and VPC options; we support private link and peering for Dedicated. We'll add security contacts to next steps.
00:07:52 Maya: Any gotchas with vector format? We're currently using float32 in FAISS. If you quantize to int8 or 4-bit what about quality loss?
00:08:03 Diego: There is some degradation depending on model and distance metric; we provide quantization profiles per model and recommend running small A/Bs. In many text retrieval tasks int8 gives negligible quality drop, 4-bit more risky but often acceptable for recall-first use. We'll include quality vs compression curves.
00:08:26 Ethan: How do you handle versioning and rollouts for rerank models? We don't want a bad reranker to degrade results in prod.
00:08:33 Ava: Redwood Console supports model version pinning and canary rollouts. You can route a percentage of requests to a new reranker and run automated evals against pre-defined prompt sets. Also rollback is immediate.
00:08:50 Maya: Nice. For our POC we'd like a small pilot: 100k docs, run our query set against bm25+embed rerank and compare to current. Can Redwood run the reranker and host vectors?
00:08:59 Diego: Yes, we can spin a Dedicated pilot or a Hosted trial with VPC-like protections. Given security constraints, Dedicated pilot with VPC peering and customer KMS seems prudent. We can set up a two-day benchmark run.
00:09:24 Jordan: What instrumentation will we get? Token-level cost maybe not relevant, but latency breakdowns, per-route metrics, and trace logs are important.
00:09:33 Ava: Redwood Console gives token-level cost, per-route latency, model-level dashboards, and traces. We'll also provide access to logs and traces for the pilot.
00:09:45 Ethan: One operational question — for rerank batching, if we batch user queries will that increase apparent latency? We have low-latency interactive use.
00:09:55 Diego: You tune batch windows. For interactive 100-200ms SLOs we recommend small max-batch latency (10-20ms) with more nodes to maintain throughput. For async or background tasks you can increase batching. It's a capacity tradeoff.
00:10:12 Maya: Any issues with multilingual docs? We have content in en, es, and pt.
00:10:18 Diego: Embedding model selection matters; some models are multilingual. We'll show model profiles; dedicated infra supports multiple models pinned per route.
00:10:30 Ava: Quick recap and proposed next steps?
00:10:34 Maya: Please send security docs, benchmarking spreadsheet, and a pilot proposal. We'll provide sample dataset and queries.
00:10:42 Ava: Action items: we'll send the security packet and benchmarks; Diego will prepare the throughput matrix for 768 vs 1536 dims; we'll propose Dedicated pilot dates.
00:10:52 Ethan: Sounds good.

Closing notes: There were a few ASR noise words and occasional speaker mislabels during calls ("Redwood Dedicate" etc). Transcript may mis-spell some product names; actual docs to be shared by Redwood.

References mentioned: Pinecone, Weaviate, FAISS, OpenSearch, BM25, HNSW, IVFPQ, KMS, SOC2.

End of transcript.
